reason:
The finding's central claim is factually false, and the behaviour it reports as a defect is a reserve that an earlier round built on purpose and that measures as working.

1) "Never once sets on one line at any width" is wrong. I drove master.html at state=owner-editing and measured .b-stepRead with a Range across 390/701/768/800/900/1000/1023/1024/1152/1279/1280/1440, at rest, after +7 x2 and after -1 x3. Across the whole 701-1023 band the sentence sets on ONE line in every content state: 336px at rest, 345.6px after +7 x2, 355.2px after -1 x3, all inside a 480px measure - 125px of slack at the longest string tested. 768 is one of the brief's own listed frames; the finding did not drive it. The two-line set occurs only at 390 (332px box) and at 1024+ (310px box), not "at any width".

2) The two-line set is the reserve, not a fault. b.css:773-782 sets min-height: 45px on .b-stepRead with the comment "Two lines reserved. Unreserved, the first press collapsed it from 45px to 23px and moved every control below it by 22px", and render-b.js:842 repeats it at the call site. The measurement confirms it holds: the box is exactly 45px tall at EVERY width - one line at 768, two lines at 1440 and 390, same 45px. The top of the .b-ceiling hint below it is identical at 768 (one line) and 390 (two lines) for the same content - 663.6px at rest, 599.6px after a step - so the readout never reflows the steppers. That is the reserve doing precisely the job it was built for, and it is why the two-line set costs nothing.

3) The hanging middot is round 7's deliberate choice, and the fix removes the wrong half of it. interaction-check.mjs:2615-2622 asserts charCodeAt(i-1) === 0x00a0 before the middot - "the connector cannot start a line". The middot ending line 1 is the intended residue of that binding; the alternative it was chosen over is the middot OPENING line 2, which is the worse of the two settings. The finding treats the accepted consequence as an unnoticed defect.

4) The proposed fix makes the artifact worse. Emitting the day and the distance as two display:block children forces a permanent break at 701-1023, destroying the best setting the component achieves - a whole, unbroken sentence with 125px to spare - to hard-code a break that is only needed at two of the seven widths driven. It also deletes the connector and forces a rewrite of a passing gate assertion in order to ship that regression. The finding's own fallback (13px --size-data) it concedes does not fit either.

5) Minor: the widow figures are also wrong. The last line is 96 against a widest line of 230.4 (ratio 0.417), not 96/240; and the widow gate is at interaction-check.mjs:1928-1948, not L1147.

Nothing here is real, specific and an improvement at a 9.5 bar.
